messages.text: Our office espresso machine is leaking. A wants a simpler one and B wants to keep the old one. I don't want a fight over coffee. Can you help us sort it out?

By a simpler machine, I mean one that’s reliable and needs little upkeep. I’d like a usable coffee setup without a repair job or cleaning rota becoming someone’s ongoing responsibility; I’m afraid I can’t take that on. I’d hope for a practical decision without a long back-and-forth.

Your three NCEs seem fair to me: let’s not use the leaking machine until it’s checked, not discard it without a clear reason, and include all three of us. I know B wants to keep it; it was our late father’s, and B brought it from home. The machine has been here for years, we all use it daily, and the grinder goes with it. I don’t know its repair history, the ownership arrangements, the office rules, or who can approve repairs or purchases—bringing it in doesn’t settle ownership.

Keeping it matters to me because it was our late father’s. I know that’s not a practical argument, but I don’t want it tossed aside casually. I want a dependable setup and want this machine repaired and kept if it’s reasonably repairable. The leak is a real safety concern, and it keeps breaking; I don’t know of a problem with the grinder. Please don’t use the machine until it’s checked.

Your three NCEs belong on the list. I’d add that repair or discussion needs to fit short time slots—I’m stretched thin, and there’s no hard deadline. I expect us to look into repair before deciding to replace it, but I don’t know costs or what’s reasonable yet.

The machine and grinder have been in the kitchen for years and we all use them daily. I don’t know the formal ownership, repair history, office rules, or who can approve spending. A and I’s father owned the machine; I can’t say who legally owns it now. Include the office manager for ownership and approval questions.

I need a dependable coffee setup, and I’d like us to keep this calm and fair. I’m not taking a side or handling the repair. I’m concerned about using a leaking machine and about replacing it without checking whether it can be repaired. I don’t know who owns it, its repair history, the office rules, or who can approve spending; please involve the office manager.

The proposed NCEs seem right to me. I’d add that the grinder should be treated separately unless someone identifies a problem with it. I don’t know of any other relevant facts.

Thanks. I agree the grinder should be treated separately; I meant it’s part of the setup, not that it needs replacing. A safety and repair check before replacing the machine, manager guidance, short time slots, and no hard deadline all seem sensible. I can’t confirm B’s repair-history concerns, and I don’t know the ownership or approval facts. C shouldn’t be expected to handle repairs, and a neutral process seems right.

The plan and written check-in sound workable, though I’d rather not take on sending the manager note. Perhaps B could send one short note, since she brought the machine in. A brief written check-in would suit me better than a kitchen debate.

Your read on the grinder is right: it goes with the machine, but I’m not asking to replace it. I agree with A’s low-upkeep and no-long-back-and-forth NCEs, and with C’s separate treatment, calm fair process, no side-taking, no repair handling, and office-manager involvement. I agree with your four NCEs too.

The plan sounds sensible. I can send the short note to the office manager in a small slot, and a written check-in works better for me than a kitchen debate.

I agree with the draft NCEs, including yours, and they state mine correctly. I agree the grinder stays separate unless a problem is identified. B can send the one short note; I’d prefer a written check-in to a kitchen debate, and I don’t want to send the note myself. The plan seems fair, provided I’m not expected to chase or handle the repair.

Thanks. I agree with the final plan. I agree that B bringing the machine in does not establish ownership; B should send the note because she offered and can manage a small slot. I have no further corrections.
I agree with the final list and plan. I’ll send the short note to the office manager and join the written check-in. The grinder entry is right.
I have no corrections or disagreements. The list and plan fit my needs; I won’t send the note or chase or handle the repair.
